data.metric: exact FP16 bit equality vs FP64 sigmoid rounded once to binary16

evidence.summary: Exhaustive sweep of all 65536 finite FP16 encodings: 7 bit-pattern mismatches vs FP64 sigmoid rounded once to binary16. Decisive case x=0.0029296875: true sigmoid 0.5007324213511315 < FP16 tie midpoint 0.500732421875, so correct output is 0x3801 (0.50048828125), but kernel outputs 0x3802 (0.5009765625). Cause: FP32 exp/div intermediate error crosses the FP16 rounding tie. All 7 failing inputs are small legal finite values (~±0.01) where the contract's round-once requirement is violated.

rationale: FP32 intermediate (libdevice exp, div_rn) then a single cvt.rn to FP16 can double-round or deviate when the true value is near an FP16 rounding tie, and libdevice.exp is not guaranteed correctly rounded. Exhaustive test over all 65536 FP16 encodings will decide.

scope_evidence.summary: Each output must be the real-value sigmoid rounded ONCE to IEEE binary16, round-to-nearest ties-to-even; 'Exact FP16 bit patterns ... must hold for the whole public domain. One failing legal input is evidence against the implementation.' All finite FP16 encodings are legal inputs.

scope_rationale: Contract requires exact FP16 bit patterns equal to single correctly-rounded sigmoid for every finite FP16 input; any bit mismatch on any of these inputs is a contract violation.
statement: The kernel's FP32 intermediate arithmetic (exp and div_rn) followed by a single FP16 round produces a bit pattern that differs from the correctly-rounded FP16 sigmoid for at least one finite FP16 input.
